thread:
carla_support: Customer reports function-call args arrive truncated when using streaming (SSE) path through our API Gateway. Payload ends mid-json and parser fails with 'Unexpected end of input'.

carla_support: Customer says it reliably fails after ~9-12s of stream; non-streaming requests are fine. They sent an example of the streamed data they received:
```
event: tool_call
data: {"tool":{"name":"charge","args":{"amount":100,"currency":"usd","order_id":"ord_5X"}
```
(the JSON is missing the trailing " ) and the final }

carla_support: They are hitting our hosted API via their reverse proxy (a managed nginx) and we see a 200 from our runtime. Customer provided request id x-request-id=zz-9c3a.

support-bot: Ticket created: #SUP-2319 (auto).

ben_prod_eng: Thanks. First questions: which client lib and node/browser? Is the customer using fetch() in Node/edge or a streaming websocket?

carla_support: They say Node 18 fetch (undici), proxy in front, TLS termination at the edge, and our hosted endpoint https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/stream.

ben_prod_eng: Two quick hypotheses: (1) proxy/nginx is buffering or cutting keepalive leading to truncated chunked stream, (2) our runtime emits SSE chunk breaks that split JSON tokens across data frames and downstream reassembly fails because client-side handler expects a single 'data:' block per event.

pri_qa: I saw a similar intermittent repro in QA with nginx default proxy_buffering enabled. If proxy_buffering is on and proxy_read_timeout triggers, the client can get a truncated chunk if the connection is closed mid-chunk.

carla_support: Customer attached nginx error log snippet: 
```
2019/12/12 12:01:01 [error] 12345#0: *6789 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.0.0.1, server: -, request: "GET /v1/stream"
```

dave_oncall: Can we reproduce internally with a proxy that applies timeouts/buffering? I'll try with nginx config: proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_buffering on; proxy_read_timeout 10s; chunked_transfer_encoding on.

ben_prod_eng: Also dump the raw bytes of the SSE stream from our edge to verify chunk boundaries. If we are splitting a JSON token across chunks we still should be fine — SSE clients reassemble per event — but if a middle proxy kills the connection while half an event is in-flight, we get exactly this.

carla_support: Customer mentioned they tried setTimeout on client side and saw last event id missing; they tried reconnect and only saw partial args again.

ben_prod_eng: Do we log streaming termination reasons on runtime? We should correlate runtime logs for the request id zz-9c3a. If runtime closed the stream with an error we might be able to fix there.

pri_qa: Quick repro steps I used: 
1) Start a tiny test server that streams a multi-kB JSON tool-call line over SSE slowly (50ms between writes).
2) Put nginx in front with small buffer/short read timeout and make a client request via node fetch.
3) Kill nginx worker after ~10s.
I got truncated event payloads identical to customer's.

ben_prod_eng: Good repro. Short-term workaround for customers: set stream=false (non-streaming) or increase proxy_read_timeout/proxy_buffering off. For us, we should make the runtime emit a final flush boundary for events and include an explicit checksum/length header for tool args so partial arrivals are detectable and can be retried.

dave_oncall: I pushed a debug build to staging that logs SSE frames and connection close reason for the request id. We'll correlate.

carla_support: Customer would prefer a fix rather than config guidance. They are on Dedicated in eu-west region but route to hosted API through their proxy.

ben_prod_eng: Action items: 
- Ben: add SSE frame boundary logging + last-event-id and close reason to runtime logs (low-risk).
- Dave: reproduce with nginx in docker and confirm whether a truncated chunk yields invalid JSON at our API Gateway vs at the client.
- Priya: add automated e2e test that simulates mid-chunk connection close and verifies we return a clean error or retry token.

ben_prod_eng: Example of problematic client-side event the customer posted (raw bytes):
```
data: {"tool":{"name":"charge","args":{"amount":100,"currency":"usd","order_id":"ord_5X"}
data: [TRUNCATED]
```
Notice missing closing braces and the next 'data:' starts in a new chunk — parser fails.

carla_support: Customer asked if we can deliver a hotfix quickly to add a server-side nepers: Content-Length-like delim for SSE events.

ben_prod_eng: Short-term patch: include an Event-ID header and ensure each SSE event is sent as a contiguous write on the runtime side (i.e., avoid fragmenting writes across multiple kernel send() calls). This reduces chance a proxy kills mid-write. Longer term: add resumable tool-call semantics (on reconnect with last-event-id resume).

dave_oncall: I've validated that with proxy_buffering off and keepalive_timeout increased the truncation disappears. Repro validated.

carla_support: I relayed the workaround to the customer and opened an internal ticket ENG-STREAM-542. Customer is temporarily disabling streaming.

support-bot: ENG ticket ENG-STREAM-542 created and assigned to ben_prod_eng.

ben_prod_eng: I'll target a small runtime change: coalesce writes for single SSE event and add an informative log when a connection is closed mid-event. Patch ETA 3 days. PR will include a test that simulates keepalive termination.

carla_support: Thanks — customer asked for ETA; I gave the 3-day window and offered the proxy config workaround. They want to be notified on the ticket.

pri_qa: I'll add the new test to our integration suite and include an nginx-based matrix to catch regressions.

ben_prod_eng: One more note: also check any edge load balancers (Cloud LB) that might apply idle timeouts; don't forget health-checks that may trigger connection resets.

carla_support: Closing loop here — will follow up after the PR.
